CFD Prime (Swing) Rules

Everything that applies to your CFD Prime (Swing) account, in one place — what you must do to pass, the limits you can’t breach, and what’s allowed.

Updated this week

These are the rules for your CFD Prime (Swing) account. Most apply in both the Challenge and the Earning Phase. We group them into two types: 

Hard rules — breaking one breaches the account: it fails and is disabled. 

Soft rules — requirements you must meet, but breaking them does not fail your account; you simply keep trading until you meet them. 

Exact limits (your Profit Target and drawdown amounts) depend on your account size and are shown in your Client Area. Some rules also depend on when the account was purchased — those dates are noted below.

What You Must Do To Pass (Objectives)

 

Profit Target  (Objective)

Reach the Profit Target set for your account size (shown in your Client Area and on the CFD product page) without breaking any rules.  

Minimum Profitable Days (Soft — No Breach)

You need at least 3 profitable trading days (accounts purchased or upgraded on or after 2 June 2025; earlier accounts need 5 trading days). A day is profitable when your account gains at least 0.5% of the initial balance, measured at the end-of-day cut-off (16:15 CT) using the lower of your balance or equity versus the previous day’s balance. Profitable days do not need to be consecutive.  

Consistency Rule (Soft — No Breach)

Applies only to 1-Phase $100K and $200K accounts (new accounts on or after 6 July 2026), in both phases. Your Best Day (single most profitable day) must not exceed 50% of your Positive Days’ Profit (the sum of all profitable days; losing days are excluded).  

 

Going over 50% does not fail your account — you simply keep trading and add profit on other days until your Best Day is 50% or less

 

Limits You Must Not Breach (Hard Rules)

 

Daily Drawdown (Hard Rule)

The most you can lose in a single day. It’s measured on your closed balance (Closed P&L, commissions included) and updated at the end of each day (16:15 CT).  

 

If your equity drops below the limit, the account is breached and permanently disabled. 

 

Example: 

On a $100,000 account with a $3,000 daily drawdown, the limit is $97,000. 

If the day closes at $97,100, the next day’s limit becomes $94,100 (previous close − $3,000). 

Maximum Drawdown (Hard Rule)

This is your overall loss limit. Your account has either a Static or a Trailing limit, depending on the account type and the date you bought it.

Static The limit is fixed, based on your starting balance, and never moves. Example: 10% on a $100,000 account gives a fixed limit of $90,000, even if your balance grows.

 

Trailing (based on End-of-Day balance) The limit moves up with your end-of-day closed balance until the limit itself reaches your starting balance. After that, it locks and doesn't move again. Example: You start at $100,000 with a 10% limit, so your limit is $90,000. Once your closed balance reaches $110,000, the limit has moved up to $100,000. It locks there and won't move any further.

 

For both types:

If your equity reaches or falls below the limit at any time, the account is breached.

Your limit doesn't move down after a payout. See CFD Prime (Swing) Rewards.

Stop-Out (Auto-Closes Positions) 

If your Margin Level falls to 100%, the system automatically closes one or more open positions to protect the account.  

Margin Used Per Trade Idea (Hard Rule*) 

The total margin across all positions in the same trade idea (one instrument, or a group of correlated instruments) is capped at 40% of your initial balance.  

Splitting trades does not reduce it.  

 

You get a reminder at 30%; a first violation triggers a warning and forced position closure; a second violation breaches the account.  

 

For accounts up to and including $50K, it is monitored manually by the Risk Team rather than automatically. 

 

Applies to CFD Prime (Swing) 1-Phase and 2-Phase $5K, $10K, $20K and $50K accounts, and CFD Prime (Swing) 2-Phase $100K accounts, created before 29/05/2026 

Applies to CFD Prime (Swing) 1-Phase $100K and $200K accounts created before 06/07/2026.  

Risk Per Trade Idea (Hard Rule*) 

The maximum potential loss across all positions in the same trade idea (based on your stop-losses, or worst-case exposure if you have none) is capped at 1.5% of your initial balance.  

 

Reminder at 1%; first violation = warning + forced closure; second = breach. Trading without stop-losses raises your calculated risk and can trigger warnings faster.  

Applies to accounts created before 29/05/2026, and continues to apply to CFD Prime 1-Phase $100K and $200K accounts regardless of creation date.  

 

For accounts up to and including $50K, it is monitored manually by the Risk Team rather than automatically. 

Inactivity (Hard Rule) 

If 21 consecutive days pass without placing a single trade, the account is considered inactive and breached.  

 

Holding a position overnight or leaving a pending order does not count as activity. The countdown starts as soon as the account is created. 

 

What’s Allowed, With Conditions 

 

Scalping (Allowed) 

Allowed on CFD Prime (Swing), including trades held for under a minute.  

What is not allowed is High-Frequency Trading, where the majority of your trades last only a few seconds or less.  

 

A single trade that closes in seconds because your stop-loss or take-profit was hit won’t breach your account, but deliberately placing stops or targets extremely close to entry as a strategy is treated as prohibited HFT-style trading.

Stop-Loss & Take-Profit (Allowed) 

Not mandatory on every trade, but strongly recommended.  

If the majority of your trades are placed without a stop-loss, the Risk Team may reach out and require you to use them.

News Trading (Allowed, With Limits)

Allowed on CFD accounts up to $50,000 (you may open and close trades during high-impact news).  

 

Not permitted on $100,000 and $200,000 accounts during the Challenge or Earning Phase.  

 

Where restricted, you may not open new trades — or have pending orders triggered — within 2 minutes before or after a high-impact release; trades already open beforehand may be closed during the window. 

Expert Advisors (EAs) (Allowed, With Limits) 

Allowed, provided they don’t copy signals that aren’t yours, scalp against the rules, run latency/reverse/hedge/arbitrage or HFT, use emulators, or trade within 2 minutes of high-impact news on $100K/$200K accounts.  

 

Accounts using prohibited EAs are denied any upgrade or payout, and the Challenge is not refunded.  

VPS (Allowed)

You may use a VPS to run your Expert Advisor. 

Hedging (Allowed, With Limits) 

Allowed within the same account for risk management (no hedging arbitrage).  

Hedging across two accounts — a BUY on one and a SELL on the other, including on correlated assets — is prohibited. 

Copy Trading   (Allowed, With Limits) 

Allowed only between accounts you own (effective 02/06/2025).  

Shared or mirrored trading between different people, or copying signals from an account that isn’t yours, is treated as a breach. 

Holding Overnight & Over The Weekend [Swing] (Allowed)

Allowed on all CFD accounts. Be mindful that price gaps when markets reopen can breach the daily drawdown.  

 

Cryptocurrency trades seven days a week on select platforms (from 7 July 2025). 

 
Prohibited Practices 

 

Gap Trading (Prohibited)

Trading to profit from price gaps is not allowed. This includes:

Opening trades within 2 hours of a market close when the market will stay closed for 2 or more hours, ahead of major news, earnings or events likely to cause a price gap.

Holding positions through corporate earnings announcements or material corporate actions when they are exposed to significant price gaps, especially announcements made before the market opens or after it closes.

Profits from this activity may be adjusted or removed, and the account may be terminated.

Grid Strategies (Prohibited) 

Not allowed. 

 
A grid strategy involves placing multiple buy and/or sell orders at predetermined price intervals, creating a series or “grid” of positions around a price level. 

 

This includes systematically adding multiple positions as the market moves up or down to profit from price fluctuations rather than using independent trade setups.  

Martingale Strategies (Prohibited)

Not allowed. 

 

A martingale strategy involves increasing the position size after a losing trade or series of losing trades, with the aim of recovering previous losses and generating a profit from a subsequent winning trade. This includes systematically increasing exposure as losses accumulate. 

High-Frequency Trading (HFT) (Prohibited)

Not allowed on any account: executing multiple trades per second, dozens of trades within a minute, rapid-fire entries and exits, or any attempt to exploit speed, latency or feed delays.  

 

Violations result in account termination.

Gambling (Prohibited)

Excessive risk-taking is prohibited — overleveraging, overexposure to one asset, one-sided bets without analysis, and hyperactive impulsive trading.  

 

Violations can lead to restricted trading privileges, revoked rewards, reduced leverage or account termination. See our full Gambling Policy for the details. 

 

Accounts & Other Rules 

 

How Many Accounts / Allocation

There is no limit on how many accounts you can purchase, all managed from one Dashboard.  

 

In the Earning Phase you can hold a maximum of 8 active Earning Accounts with a combined initial balance cap of $400,000. Example: if you pass three $200,000 Challenges, only two can convert to Earning Accounts ($400,000 total); the third stays pending until an active Earning Account closes or breaches.

Scaling Up

Your Earning Account balance can increase by 25% of its starting balance every 4 months, up to a combined $2,000,000 across your CFD Intraday and Prime (Swing) accounts. CFD Instant accounts (up to 2) aren't counted towards it.

 

•      What do I need to qualify? You need all of the following: at least 4 months of trading since you received the account or since its last scale-up, a net profit of at least 10% of the starting balance in that period, at least 2 processed payouts in that period, and the account in profit at the time of the scale-up.

For the Challenge to register as passed you must place a trade on at least 3 unique trading days.

Applies to the Challenge only — never to a Futures Earning Account — and it never fails your account. Your highest trading day is capped at 40% of your Profit Target; going over simply raises the target.  

 

How the new target is calculated depends on when your account was created: 

Created on or after 14 July 2026 — the target is recalculated so your highest day equals 40% of it (Highest Day ÷ 0.40 = new target). Example: a $1,500 best day on a $3,000 target → $3,750. 

Created before 14 July 2026 — the amount over the 40% cap is added to the target. Example: on a $3,000 target the cap is $1,200; a $1,500 best day is $300 over, so the target becomes $3,300. 

 

Limits You Must Not Breach (Hard Rules)
  
Max Drawdown (Trailing On End-Of-Day Balance) (Hard Rule)

Your Max Drawdown (see the table) trails your end-of-day balance — based on closed P&L, not intraday peaks — upward, until it reaches your starting balance, then locks.  

 

If your balance falls to the drawdown level, the account is breached. 

 

Example: 

$100,000 account with a $3,000 Max Drawdown → initial level $97,000. 

End-of-day balance rises to $102,000 → level trails to $99,000. 

End-of-day balance reaches $103,000 → level locks at $100,000 (your starting balance) and won’t trail higher. 

Daily Pause (Daily Loss Limit) (Auto-Close For The Day)

The Daily Pause is your maximum daily loss (see the table). When your loss reaches it, the system closes all open positions and pauses trading until the next trading day.  

The limit updates daily at 16:15 CT and is shown on your dashboard. 

 

Applies during the Challenge phase only. It was removed from Futures Prime Earning accounts on 14 July 2026. 

 

Important: the Daily Pause is a safety feature, not a guaranteed hard stop. In fast markets, slippage can push your loss past the Daily Pause — and past your Max Drawdown, which breaches the account.  

 

Do not use the Daily Pause as a substitute for a stop-loss. 

No Overnight Or Weekend Positions (Force-Closed)

Holding positions overnight is not allowed on Futures Prime.  

 

Any position still open 5 minutes before the market close (14:55 CT) is force-closed by our Risk Team.

Maximum Contracts (Position Limit) 

Your maximum position size depends on your account: 

$50K → 5 standard / 50 micro

$100K → 10 / 100

$150K → 15 / 150

There is no minimum, and the lower your current balance, the fewer contracts you’re allowed to trade.  

Inactivity (Hard Rule)

If 21 consecutive days pass without placing a single trade, the account is considered inactive and breached.  

 

Holding a position overnight or leaving a pending order doesn’t count as activity, and the countdown starts as soon as the account is purchased. 

 

What’s Allowed, With Conditions 

  

News Trading (Allowed)

Allowed on Futures Prime in both the Challenge and Earning Phase.  

Be mindful of the heightened volatility and large, unpredictable price swings around high-impact news.  
​
​Important: While news trading is permitted on Futures Prime accounts, traders are expected to maintain a disciplined and professional approach to risk management. 

If our Risk Team identifies a consistent pattern of trading exclusively around news events in a way that resembles gambling behavior, excessive risk-taking, or an attempt to exploit extreme market volatility rather than sustainable trading performance, the Risk Team reserves the right to review the account and take appropriate measures in accordance with our Terms & Conditions.

Stop-Loss & Take-Profit (Allowed)

Not mandatory on every trade, but strongly recommended.  

 

If the majority of your trades are placed without a stop-loss, the Risk Team may reach out and require you to use them. 

Copy Trading (Allowed, With Limits) 

You may copy trades, manually or automatically, across up to 5 of your own Challenges or 5 of your own Earning accounts.

 

You may only copy from your own accounts. Copying from other traders or sources is prohibited. Copying between Futures Challenges and Futures Earning accounts is allowed.

 

Running the same strategy across more than 5 accounts can lead to upgrades being denied.

 

If you use a trade copier, you're responsible for it.

•      Any software errors, malfunctions or unintended trades caused by the copier are your responsibility. If the copier fails, you'll need to troubleshoot or fix the tool on your side.

•      Account resets or balance adjustments are not given for individual technical issues. Only verified firm-wide outages affecting many traders may qualify.

Prohibited Practices 

 

Hedging (Prohibited)

A BUY and a SELL held at the same time is prohibited. 

 

Hedging involves holding a BUY and a SELL position on the same instrument simultaneously, so the two positions offset each other and the net market exposure is removed. This includes opposing positions in a single account, a BUY on one account and a SELL on another, and offsetting positions opened in correlated instruments across accounts. 

 

Micro-Scalping (Prohibited)

The Trading Pit prohibits micro-scalping because it exploits execution mechanics rather than reflecting genuine market participation. Traders are expected to use realistic, scalable strategies that can be applied consistently in live markets.

 

• What is micro-scalping? Targeting very small price moves with large position sizes and holding trades for only a few seconds.

 

• Is all scalping prohibited? No. Short-term trading based on market conditions with realistic execution is allowed. It's prohibited when results depend on execution mechanics and wouldn't transfer to real markets.

 

• How is it detected? Automated monitoring flags accounts where, for example, over 50% of profits come from trades held 15 seconds or less, or where ultra-fast entries and exits are combined with disproportionate sizing.

 

• What happens if flagged? The account undergoes manual review. Confirmed violations may result in a warning, profit removal, restrictions, or permanent closure.

 

High-Frequency Trading (HFT) (Prohibited)

Not allowed on any account: executing multiple trades per second, dozens of trades within a minute, rapid-fire entries and exits, or any attempt to exploit speed, latency or feed delays.  

Violations result in account termination. 

 

 

Accounts & Other Rules 

 

How Many Accounts 

There is no limit on how many Futures accounts you can purchase.  

 

In the Earning Phase you can hold a maximum of 5 active Earning accounts; if you pass a Challenge while already at the cap, the upgrade is queued until one of your Earning accounts closes. 

Trading Device, IP & Network

An IP that changes every few days (e.g. while travelling) is fine.

 

An IP that changes several times within the same day can raise suspicion of account sharing, which is forbidden. 

 

See our Trading Device, IP & Network Policy for the full rules on devices, IPs and shared access.

 
Account Rolling

 

What Account Rolling Means

Account rolling is the practice of using an account as a one-time bet and not as a trading strategy. It usually follows this sequence:

1.   An all-in first move. Early in the funded phase, the trader opens an outsized position that uses most or all of the available drawdown. The outcome depends on a single move in the market.

2.   If the trade works, most of the account's profit (more than 40%) comes from that one trade or day.

3.   Then the account is run at minimum effort. The trader switches to very small positions or short, fixed-target trades, often one per day, placed only to reach the minimum daily profit and complete the required number of profitable days.

4.   If the trade fails, the account reaches its Max Drawdown, and the trader moves to a new account and repeats the same approach until a bet pays off.

The cost of a failed attempt to the trader is the product fee. The cost of a successful attempt is paid by the firm. This is why we treat it as a misuse of the program and not as trading.

Common Signs

•      One trade or one day produces more than 40% of the net profit.

•      Position size drops sharply right after the large result, often from a full contract to micro contracts.

•      The remaining profitable days are consistently just above the minimum daily profit requirement.

•      The later trades repeat the same size, the same point target or the same profit amount.

•      The same approach appears on multiple accounts.

No single sign is decisive. We review the whole picture.

Why It Is Not Allowed

•      It is gambling, not skill. A result that depends on one all-or-nothing trade does not show that a trader can manage risk over time.

•      It does not meet the purpose of the reward rules. The profitable day requirement exists to measure consistent performance. Padding the remaining days to reach the minimum meets the rule on paper, but not in substance.

Account rolling falls under Clause 6.4 and Schedule B of our Terms & Conditions (Prohibited Trading Practices). It is also an impermissible risk allocation and an excessive concentration on a very small number of trades under Clause 6.5.1.

What We Expect From You

We expect a consistent, repeatable strategy with proportional market risk, with profit built across your trading days rather than concentrated in a single trade or day. Traders who trade this way have no problem receiving their payouts.

What Happens If We Identify Account Rolling?

Under Clause 6.7 of our Terms & Conditions, measures can include:

•      Removal of the offending trades and exclusion of their results from the assessment of your payout request (Clause 6.7.2).

•      Denial of the related payout request.

•      Termination of the affected accounts, or of all associated accounts, for confirmed breaches (Clause 6.7.4).

•      Permanent denial of access to our Services after repeated breaches following notice (Clause 6.7.5).

If a profit removal brings the account balance below the Max Drawdown level, the account is automatically breached. If the balance stays above that level, you can keep trading.

 Example: if you buy at $50.10, you must sell at $50.20 or higher.

Example:

A grid strategy involves placing multiple buy and/or sell orders at predetermined price intervals, creating a series or “grid” of positions around a price level. 

 

This includes systematically adding multiple positions as the market moves up or down to profit from price fluctuations rather than using independent trade setups.

Martingale Strategies (Prohibited)

A martingale strategy involves increasing the position size after a losing trade or series of losing trades, with the aim of recovering previous losses and generating a profit from a subsequent winning trade. This includes systematically increasing exposure as losses accumulate.

Maximum Drawdown (Hard Breach)

Your maximum drawdown is $2,000 on a $50,000 account and $3,500 on a $100,000 account. It's calculated on your end-of-day (EOD) balance and works on a trailing-to-static model: the drawdown level trails your highest EOD balance upward until it reaches your starting balance, then locks there and stops trailing. If your balance falls to the drawdown level, the account is breached.

 

Example ($50,000 account):

•      Starting balance $50,000 → initial drawdown level $48,000.

•      You end the day at $51,000 → level trails to $49,000.

•      You end a later day at $52,000 → level reaches $50,000 (your starting balance) and locks there — it won't trail higher even if your balance keeps rising.

Daily Pause (Dynamic)

Your Daily Pause starts at $1,200 on a $50,000 account and $2,200 on a $100,000 account. It is dynamically recalculated daily as 60% of your best accumulated EOD profit to date. It only ever increases as your profit grows.

 

If your loss for the day reaches your Daily Pause, your open positions are closed and trading is paused until the next day. Your account is not breached.

 

Example ($50,000 account):

•      Until your accumulated EOD profit passes $2,000, your Daily Pause stays at $1,200 (60% of $2,000 = $1,200).

•      Your accumulated EOD profit reaches $2,300 → Daily Pause rises to $1,380.

•      You lose $300 the next day (accumulated profit $2,000) → Daily Pause stays at $1,380. It never decreases.

•      Your accumulated EOD profit reaches a new high of $2,900 → Daily Pause rises to $1,740

•      $50,000 account: up to 4 Mini or 40 Micro contracts.

•      $100,000 account: up to 8 Mini or 80 Micro contracts.

 

Consistency

 

20% Consistency Rule (Blocks Payouts)

Your biggest profitable day must not exceed 20% of your total profit before you request a payout.

The rule resets after every approved payout.

 

Example:

•      Biggest profitable day $600 ÷ 0.20 = $3,000 total profit required.

Profit Target (Payout Requirement)

To request a reward, you need at least $3,000 profit on a $50,000 account or $6,000 on a $100,000 account. If you haven't stayed within the 20% Consistency Rule, your profit target may increase. Your dashboard always shows your current profit target.

 

Trading conditions

 

Overnight & Weekend Holding (Not Allowed)

Futures Instant is intraday only. Positions can't be held overnight or over the weekend. The daily trading session runs from 17:00 CT to 15:55 CT, and any position still open at the end of the session is closed automatically.

News Trading (Allowed)

Allowed on all Futures Instant accounts.

 

Be mindful of the heightened volatility and large, unpredictable price swings around high-impact news.

 

Important: While news trading is permitted on Futures Instant accounts, traders are expected to maintain a disciplined and professional approach to risk management. If our Risk Team identifies a consistent pattern of trading exclusively around news events in a way that resembles gambling behavior, excessive risk-taking, or an attempt to exploit extreme market volatility rather than sustainable trading performance, the Risk Team reserves the right to review the account and take appropriate measures in accordance with our Terms & Conditions.

Copy Trading (Allowed, With Limits)

You can copy trades between your own two Futures Instant accounts.

Shared or mirrored trading between different users, or copying signals from an account that isn't yours, is strictly prohibited.

 

If you use a trade copier, you're responsible for it.

 

•      Any software errors, malfunctions or unintended trades caused by the copier are your responsibility. If the copier fails, you'll need to troubleshoot or fix the tool on your side.

•      Account resets or balance adjustments are not given for individual technical issues. Only verified firm-wide outages affecting many traders may qualify.

Inactivity (Hard Breach)

If no trade is placed for 14 days, the account is breached.

 

Prohibited practices

 

Hedging — Opposing Positions (Strictly Prohibited)

The Trading Pit prohibits hedging across accounts to ensure fair trading conditions, accurate performance evaluation, and compliance with CME exchange standards. Traders are expected to maintain genuine market exposure at all times.

 

•      What's not allowed? Holding opposing positions across accounts you own or control, or coordinating opposite trades with another trader.

•      Does it include related instruments? Yes, correlated products count too (e.g., NQ vs. MNQ, ES vs. MES), even with different contract sizes.

•      What are the consequences? Position closure, account liquidation, profit removal, and possible permanent bans, even if unintentional.

Micro-Scalping (Prohibited)

The Trading Pit prohibits micro-scalping because it exploits execution mechanics rather than reflecting genuine market participation. Traders are expected to use realistic, scalable strategies that can be applied consistently in live markets.

 

•      What is micro-scalping? Targeting very small price moves with large position sizes and holding trades for only a few seconds.

 

•      Is all scalping prohibited? No. Short-term trading based on market conditions with realistic execution is allowed. It's prohibited when results depend on execution mechanics and wouldn't transfer to real markets.

 

•      How is it detected? Automated monitoring flags accounts where, for example, over 50% of profits come from trades held 15 seconds or less, or where ultra-fast entries and exits are combined with disproportionate sizing.

 

•      What happens if flagged? The account undergoes manual review. Confirmed violations may result in a warning, profit removal, restrictions, or permanent closure.

High-Frequency Trading (HFT) (Prohibited)

The Trading Pit prohibits high-frequency trading to protect platform stability, ensure fair access for all traders, and support strategies that reflect real-world market conditions. Trading should demonstrate skill-based decision-making rather than speed or technological advantage.

 

•      What is HFT? Automated or algorithmic trading that submits large numbers of orders within seconds or milliseconds to capture small price discrepancies.

 

•      Why is it prohibited? It strains platform infrastructure, creates speed-based advantages over other traders, and can distort execution data.

 

•      How is it detected? Monitoring systems flag exceptionally high order volume, rapid placement and cancellation cycles, and activity inconsistent with manual trading.

 

•      What happens if flagged? The account undergoes internal review. Confirmed violations may result in a warning, profit removal, account closure, or permanent loss of access.

Can I Cancel And Get A Refund After Buying A Challenge?

If you’re a consumer, you have a legal right to withdraw from your purchase within 14 days — but only for as long as you haven’t started. 
​
If you're a consumer, you have a legal right to withdraw from your purchase within 14 days, but only for as long as you haven't started.

 

The moment you open your first demo trade, you're asking us to begin the service straight away. The service is then treated as fully delivered, and the right of withdrawal is lost.

 

After that point, the Product Fee is non-refundable. In particular, there's no refund if you end a Challenge early, don't meet the Product Objectives, are terminated for good cause that's down to you, or the account expires through inactivity. Business (entrepreneur) customers don't have this statutory right of withdrawal.

 

To withdraw in time: email support@thetradingpit.com with a clear statement that you're withdrawing, before you place your first trade (or use the withdrawal function on the website, if available).

 

This doesn't affect your mandatory statutory rights, for example a refund or price reduction if a Product has a genuine defect.

 

As an exception, The Trading Pit may issue a refund as a goodwill gesture in cases where outdated documentation has caused confusion or misinformation.

 

This reflects the company's commitment to fairness and transparency, and such discrepancies are promptly addressed by updating the relevant documentation to prevent future misunderstandings.

 

Once a refund has been issued for an account, it cannot be reactivated. Customers who wish to trade again after receiving a refund must purchase a new Challenge through their Client Area. This ensures clarity and consistency in account management practices.


​

What About Chargebacks?

If you think a charge is wrong, contact support@thetradingpit.com first. 

 

Don’t raise a chargeback with your bank or card provider on a legitimate charge: a chargeback that is fraudulent or malicious is a breach of contract. 

 

We can stop the affected service immediately, claim damages, and it can lead to your account being terminated. 

Breached, Terminated, Or Closed — What’s The Difference?

“My account is closed” can mean very different things. These three are not the same: 

Term 

	

What it means 




Breached 

	

Your trading account (a Challenge or Earning account) failed because you broke a rule or hit a drawdown limit. That trading account is disabled — but your Client Account (profile) stays open, and you can start a new Challenge. 




Terminated 

	

We end a Product Contract. Either side can end one with 7 days’ notice, and we can end it immediately for good cause (see below). 




Closed 

	

You close your entire Client Account — your whole Trading Pit profile. All your accounts and contracts then end. 

Quick guide: 

“my account failed after a trade” = breached·  

“you ended my account” = terminated·  

“I want to remove my whole profile” = closed. 

 

What Does “Breached” Mean, And How Do I Check Why?

A breach means a trading account failed a rule — most often a drawdown limit, a prohibited practice, or a rule broken while reaching the Profit Target.  

 

Your Client Account isn’t affected, and you can buy another Challenge. To see the exact reason, log in to your dashboard, open the account, and read the breach reason shown next to the account number.  

 

Each product’s rules article explains its specific limits.

When Can My Account Be Terminated?

Either you or we can end a Product Contract at any time, without reason, with 7 days’ notice.  

 

We can also end it immediately for good cause — for example: not meeting the access requirements, non-payment, breaking the trading rules, an abusive chargeback, failing or not completing KYC (or giving false information), breaching multiple accounts, a legal or regulatory risk, or any other material breach. 

How Do I Dispute A Breach Or A Decision?

If an automated or Risk-Team decision affected your account — for example a breach — you can ask for a human to review it.  
​

You have the right to request human intervention, put across your point of view, and contest the decision. We’ll review it without undue delay and let you know the outcome within 30 days (extended by up to 60 more days only if the case is especially complex, and we’ll tell you if so).

How To Raise

First, check the breach reason in your dashboard so you know exactly what you’re disputing. 

Email support@thetradingpit.com with your account number and a clear explanation of what happened and why you think the decision should be reviewed. 

We’ll confirm we’ve received it and come back to you with the outcome within the timeframe above.

How Do I Close My Client Account?

First, make sure this is what you mean. This is about closing your entire Client Account (your Trading Pit profile). If instead your trading account stopped working after a rule breach, that’s a breach, not a closure — see the section above. 

 

To close it, email support@thetradingpit.com from the address on your account.  

 

When your Client Account is closed, all of your active demo trading accounts and Product Contracts end immediately, and any Product Fees already paid are not refunded.

How we define excessive risk-taking, and the responsible-trading practices we expect. Applies to all The Trading Pit products.

October 2, 2026

At The Trading Pit, we are committed to promoting safe and responsible trading. This Gambling Policy sets out the practices we treat as excessive risk-taking, and is written to be clear and accessible to all traders. Its purpose is to establish responsible trading practices and discourage actions that resemble gambling. 

 

We caution traders against chasing fast earnings — such actions are risky. We encourage a focus on gradual, consistent trading that protects both the trader and the stability of the company. “Gambling” is the term we use for actions that violate this policy; every trader is expected to take a disciplined, well-calculated approach and steer clear of overly risky behaviour. 

 

Forbidden Gambling Practices 

Overleveraging — excessive leverage is restricted. Use stop-loss orders and appropriate trade sizes to control and limit potential losses. 

 

Overexposure — don’t over-concentrate on specific assets or markets. A diversified approach is essential for mitigating risk. 

 

One-Sided Bets — avoid trading predominantly in one direction without proper market analysis. Every decision should be informed and supported by research.

 

Hyperactivity — avoid placing too many trades in a short time or acting impulsively. Focus on well-thought-out trades that fit your plan and risk tolerance. 

Risk-Management We Expect 

Maximum Risk Allocation — avoid committing a large share of your balance or equity to open positions. Balanced allocation is key to managing risk.

 

Position Sizing — size each trade with market conditions, your risk appetite and pre-set stop-losses in mind, so activity stays within manageable risk.

 

Diversification — spread across different assets, strategies and timeframes to mitigate risk. 

 

Regular Review and Adjustment — review and adjust your positions and strategies as market conditions, economic indicators and news change.

 

Education and Awareness — keep learning about market trends, new strategies and risk-management techniques to support informed decisions.

Monitoring & Consequences 

We actively monitor all trading activity for adherence to this policy. Violations can lead to restricted trading privileges, the revocation of any rewards generated through the violation, reduced leverage or, in severe cases, account termination.

What Is The CFD Prime (Swing) Reward Policy? 

On CFD Prime (Swing) you can receive a reward of up to 80% of the notional profit generated in your Earning Account, with a minimum reward of $100 per request.

When Can I Request A Reward? 

Your first reward can be requested 14 days after you receive your Earning Account. 

 

After that, you can request every 14 days for amounts above $100.

 

Reward requests are processed daily, Monday to Friday, within 24 hours on business days. 

Does A Payout Affect My Maximum Drawdown?

Yes. Your Maximum Drawdown limit doesn't move down after a payout, and there's no cap on how much you can request. If your balance reaches the limit after a payout, the account is breached, so it's your responsibility to leave enough buffer when you choose how much to request.

 

Trailing accounts: once your limit has locked at your starting balance, requesting your full profit brings your balance down to the limit and breaches the account. Example: your balance is $110,000 and your limit is locked at $100,000. Requesting your full $10,000 profit drops your balance to $100,000 and breaches the account. Requesting $6,000 leaves your balance at $104,000, with a $4,000 buffer.

 

Static accounts: a payout alone can't breach your account, because you can only withdraw profit and your limit is below your starting balance. Your buffer still gets smaller after every payout. Example: your balance is $110,000 and your limit is $90,000. After a $10,000 payout, your balance is $100,000 and you have a $10,000 buffer.

 

For how each drawdown type works, see Maximum Drawdown in CFD Prime Rules.

 

Trading Requirements Before A Reward 

Accounts created after 6 March 2026: at least 3 profitable trading days, each gaining at least 0.5% of the initial balance. 

 

Accounts created before 6 March 2026: at least 5 trading days, regardless of outcome. If most of the profit was made on the first day, you must keep trading with the same approach or the reward may be declined by the Risk Team. 

Accounts created after 5 July 2026 (CFD 1-Phase $100K/$200K): the 50% Consistency Rule must also be met. [Latest]

Transfer Timeframes 

Crypto: within the day. 

 

International wire / SWIFT: 5–7 business days. 

 

SEPA transfer: 1–3 business days.

Can I Withdraw Anything I Make During The Challenge? 

No. Trading in the Challenge takes place on a demo account with simulated funds, so there is nothing to withdraw — the Challenge only proves your trading against the targets and rules.  

 

You can request rewards only after you pass and move to the Earning Phase.

Can I Get A Refund After I Move To The Earning Phase? 

Yes, once you reach the Earning Phase your Challenge fee can be refunded, based on when the account was purchased.  

 

Accounts purchased before 29 April 2026: refunded after your 1st payout is approved.  

 

Accounts purchased on or after 29 April 2026: refunded after your 3rd payout.  

The refund is tied to successful performance in the Earning Phase — if the payout milestone isn’t met, the refund isn’t issued. 

Are There Any Reward Fees? 

To cover transaction/gas fees, a 1% fee is deducted from the trader receiving the payout. It is calculated on your final reward share amount, not on the total profit made in the account. 

In What Currency Can I Receive My Reward? 

Accounts are supported in Euro, US Dollar (for bank transfers) and Cryptocurrency, and rewards can be paid in a range of currencies.  

 

You choose your preferred method and currency when submitting the request.  

If you pick a currency other than EUR or USD, the amount is converted at the exchange rate on the day of the transaction. 

What Withdrawal Methods Are Available, And Can I Receive Rewards In Crypto? 

We currently support bank wire transfers and cryptocurrency for reward withdrawals, with more methods coming.  

 

For bank wires you’ll be asked to upload documentation showing the bank name, branch, account number and account holder’s name.

How Many Lots Can I Trade? 

There is no hard limit on lots. Your maximum position size is limited by the margin each instrument requires: the more margin your positions use, the fewer additional lots you can open. 

 

Margin = (Volume × Contract Size × Asset Price) ÷ Leverage. For example, 1 lot of EUR/USD at 1.1000 with 1:50 leverage and a 100,000 contract size requires (1 × 100,000 × 1.1000) ÷ 50 = 2,200 USD margin. 

 

As guidance, keep margin use below 30% per trade idea and risk below 1.5%.

Can I Trade Spot Forex In The CFD Challenges? 

No. We do not offer Spot Forex in the CFD Challenges — only CFDs. 

The Chart Price Never Reached My Order — Why Was It Executed? 

A chart shows two prices: the bid and the ask, and the difference between them is the spread.  

 

By default the chart displays the bid price, but buy orders fill at the ask and sell orders fill at the bid.  

 

So the visible (bid) price may not appear to reach your level even though the ask has already triggered your order. To see both, right-click the chart, open Properties, and enable “Show Ask price line”.

What You Must Do To Pass (Objectives)

Minimum Profitable Days / Trading Days (Soft — No Breach)

•      All 2-Phase accounts and 1-Phase $2,500 to $50,000: at least 3 profitable days. A day is profitable when your account gains at least 0.5% of the initial balance, measured at the 16:15 CT end-of-day cut-off.

•      1-Phase $100,000 and $200,000: at least 3 trading days. These days don't need to be profitable.

The days don't need to be consecutive.

Consistency Rule (Soft — No Breach)

Applies to 1-Phase $100,000 and $200,000 accounts only, in both phases. Your Best Day (your single most profitable day) must not exceed 50% of your Positive Days' Profit (the sum of all your profitable days; losing days are excluded).

Going over 50% doesn't fail the account. Keep trading and add profit on other days until your Best Day is 50% or less.

Daily Loss Limit (Hard Rule)

This is the maximum loss allowed in a single day: 3% on 1-Phase accounts and 5% on 2-Phase accounts. It's measured on your end-of-day balance (closed P&L, commissions included) and updated at the end of each day at 16:15 CT. If your equity drops below the limit, the account is breached.

Example (2-Phase $100,000 account):

•      5% daily loss limit = $5,000 → today's limit is $95,000.

•      If the day closes at $96,100, tomorrow's limit becomes $91,100.

Maximum Loss (Hard Rule)

This is your overall loss limit. Which version applies depends on your account:

•      Static — 1-Phase $2,500 to $50,000 (6%) and every 2-Phase account (10%). The limit is fixed from your initial balance and never moves. Example: 10% on a 2-Phase $100,000 account is a fixed $90,000 limit, however much your balance grows.

•      Trailing on end-of-day balance — 1-Phase $100,000 and $200,000 (10%). The limit moves up with your end-of-day balance until it reaches your starting balance, then locks. Example: on a $100,000 account, once your closed balance reaches $110,000, the limit fixes at $100,000 and stops moving.

In both versions, if your equity falls below the limit at any time, the account is breached.

No Overnight Or Weekend Holding (Auto-Closes Positions)

CFD Intraday is for day trading. Close all your positions 10 minutes before market close, and don't hold positions over the weekend.

Any position still open at the end of an instrument's trading session is closed automatically by the system. This also applies to crypto, on a daily basis. You can check each instrument's trading session directly in the trading platform.

If you want to hold positions overnight or over the weekend, choose Swing at checkout.

Stop-Out (Auto-Closes Positions)

If your Margin Level falls to 100%, the system automatically closes one or more open positions to protect your account.

Do The Margin And Risk Per Trade Idea Rules Apply?

No. The Margin Used Per Trade Idea and Risk Per Trade Idea rules don't apply to CFD Intraday.

Inactivity (Hard Rule)

If 21 consecutive days pass without a single trade, the account is considered inactive and breached. Leaving a pending order doesn't count as activity. The countdown starts when the account is created.

 

What's Allowed, With Conditions

 

News Trading (Allowed In The Challenge Only)

News trading is allowed during the Challenge.

In the Earning Phase, it isn't allowed. Trading is blocked from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after major news releases, so make sure you're flat (no open positions) during that window.

Scalping (Allowed)

Allowed, including trades held for under a minute. What isn't allowed is High-Frequency Trading, where the majority of your trades last only a few seconds or less.

A single trade that closes in seconds because your stop-loss or take-profit was hit won't breach your account, but deliberately placing stops or targets extremely close to entry as a strategy is treated as prohibited HFT-style trading.

Stop-Loss & Take-Profit (Allowed)

Not mandatory on every trade, but strongly recommended. If the majority of your trades are placed without a stop-loss, the Risk Team may contact you and require you to use them.

Expert Advisors (EAs) (Allowed, With Limits)

Allowed, provided they don't copy signals that aren't yours, scalp against the rules, run latency, reverse, hedge, arbitrage or HFT strategies, use emulators, or trade high-impact news in the Earning Phase. Accounts using prohibited EAs are denied any upgrade or payout, and the Challenge is not refunded.

VPS (Allowed)

You may use a VPS to run your Expert Advisor.

Hedging (Allowed, With Limits)

Allowed within the same account for risk management (no hedging arbitrage). Hedging across two accounts — a BUY on one and a SELL on the other, including on correlated assets — is prohibited.

Copy Trading (Allowed, With Limits)

Allowed only between accounts you own. Shared or mirrored trading between different people, or copying signals from an account that isn't yours, is treated as a breach.

 

Prohibited Practices

 

Gap Trading (Prohibited)

Trading to profit from price gaps is not allowed. This includes:

Opening trades within 2 hours of a market close when the market will stay closed for 2 or more hours, ahead of major news, earnings or events likely to cause a price gap.

Holding positions through corporate earnings announcements or material corporate actions when they are exposed to significant price gaps, especially announcements made before the market opens or after it closes.

Profits from this activity may be adjusted or removed, and the account may be terminated.

Grid Strategies (Prohibited)

Not allowed.

A grid strategy involves placing multiple buy and/or sell orders at predetermined price intervals, creating a series or "grid" of positions around a price level.

This includes systematically adding multiple positions as the market moves up or down to profit from price fluctuations rather than using independent trade setups.

Martingale Strategies (Prohibited)

Not allowed.

A martingale strategy involves increasing the position size after a losing trade or series of losing trades, with the aim of recovering previous losses and generating a profit from a subsequent winning trade. This includes systematically increasing exposure as losses accumulate.

High-Frequency Trading (HFT) (Prohibited)

Not allowed on any account: executing multiple trades per second, dozens of trades within a minute, rapid-fire entries and exits, or any attempt to exploit speed, latency or feed delays. Violations result in account termination.

Gambling (Prohibited)

Excessive risk-taking is prohibited — overleveraging, overexposure to one asset, one-sided bets without analysis, and hyperactive impulsive trading. Violations can lead to restricted trading privileges, revoked rewards, reduced leverage or account termination. See our full Gambling Policy for the details.

 

Accounts & Other Rules

 

How Many Accounts / Allocation

There's no limit on how many Challenges you can buy, and all accounts are managed from one Dashboard.

In the Earning Phase, you can have up to 8 active Earning Accounts, with a combined initial balance of up to $400,000. This limit is shared across your CFD Intraday, Swing and Prime accounts. CFD Instant accounts (up to 2) aren't counted towards it.

Scaling Up

Your Earning Account balance can increase by 25% of its starting balance every 4 months, up to a combined $2,000,000 across your CFD Intraday and Prime (Swing) accounts. CFD Instant accounts (up to 2) aren't counted towards it.

 

•      What do I need to qualify? You need all of the following: at least 4 months of trading since you received the account or since its last scale-up, a net profit of at least 10% of the starting balance in that period, at least 2 processed payouts in that period, and the account in profit at the time of the scale-up.

•      How do I get it? Submit a scale-up request. Our Risk team reviews it and approves or declines it.

•      How much is added? 25% of the original starting balance each time. It doesn't compound, so a $100,000 account grows by $25,000 at every scale-up. If a scale-up would take you over $2,000,000, only the amount up to the limit is added.

•      What happens to my loss limits? They keep the same percentages and are recalculated on your new balance.

•      Are my accounts assessed separately? Yes. Each account must qualify on its own, and accounts can't be merged. Only the $2,000,000 limit is combined.

Trading Device, IP & Network

Trade from your own personal device, don't share it, and don't access more than one account from the same IP address or network. You can trade from anywhere and switch networks freely, and VPNs are allowed as long as they aren't used to share access or hide coordinated activity. Read the full policy.

How Can I Check Why My Account Has Been Breached?

Log in to your Client Area, select Accounts and click the account number. The reason for the breach is shown at the top centre of the account's Dashboard, next to the account number.

CFD Intraday Rewards

How and when you get your rewards on CFD Intraday: reward share, requests, trading requirements, refunds, fees and methods.

Updated this week
What Is The CFD Intraday Reward Policy?

You can receive a reward of up to 80% of the notional profit in your Earning Account. The minimum reward is $100 per request.

When Can I Request A Reward?

Your first reward can be requested 14 days after you receive your Earning Account. After that, you can request a reward every 14 days, for any amount above $100. Requests are processed daily, Monday to Friday, within 24 hours on business days.

Trading Requirements Before A Reward

•      All 2-Phase accounts and 1-Phase $2,500 to $50,000: at least 3 profitable trading days, each gaining at least 0.5% of the initial balance.

•      1-Phase $100,000 and $200,000: at least 3 trading days, and the 50% Consistency Rule must be met.

•      No news trading in the Earning Phase.

Transfer Timeframes

•      Crypto: within the day.

•      International wire / SWIFT: 5–7 business days.

•      SEPA transfer: 1–3 business days.

Can I Withdraw Anything I Make During The Challenge?

No. The Challenge is traded on a demo account with simulated funds, so there's nothing to withdraw. You can request rewards only after you pass the Challenge and move to the Earning Phase.

Can I Get A Refund After I Move To The Earning Phase?

Yes. Once you reach the Earning Phase, your Challenge fee is refunded after your 3rd approved payout. If you don't reach that payout milestone, no refund is issued.

Are There Any Reward Fees?

A 1% fee is deducted from your payout to cover transaction and gas fees. It's calculated on your final reward share amount, not on your total account profit.

In What Currency Can I Receive My Reward?

Accounts are supported in EUR, USD (for bank transfers) and cryptocurrency. You choose the method and currency when you submit your request. Currencies other than EUR or USD are converted at the exchange rate on the day of the transaction.

What Withdrawal Methods Are Available?

Rewards are paid by bank wire or cryptocurrency. For bank wires, you'll need documentation showing the bank name, branch, account number and account holder's name.
